observations.summary: The shortcut state model is default-plus-override, persisted in GuiConfig, rebuilt at defined lifecycle points, and installed into key-event routing.
The skills backend is PM-native: it discovers canonical and compatible roots, validates tool references, bundles selected content, and exposes on-demand retrieval.
Projection ownership and failure state are explicitly separated from PM-native runtime delivery.
Shortcut filtering and skill validation have concrete user-visible empty, success, and per-item failure behavior.
Cleanup is designed as a centralized module with pre-execution preparation, post-execution cleanup, and a prohibition on post-run git-clean behavior.
The subsection declares implementation-plan readiness and says open choices are resolved or deliberately scoped.

candidate_findings.summary: Duplicate shortcut handling is contradictory: backend validation mandates rejection, while edit and import behavior still permit either rejection or stealing the binding. This leaves whether an existing action is mutated or preserved unspecified.

The export payload is not exact. The acceptance summary promises export of current overrides, but the detailed flow permits either overrides or the full effective key map, producing materially different restore and sharing behavior.

Import compatibility is unresolved: missing or future versions can be rejected or parsed best-effort, and unknown action identifiers can be skipped or reject the entire import. The atomicity and forward-compatibility contract therefore remain discretionary.

The cross-platform KeyBinding representation is not fixed. macOS mapping may occur while reading, writing, or displaying configuration, while serialization can be string or structured and export examples use Ctrl tokens. The canonical stored token space and round-trip mapping are unspecified.

Shortcut persistence failure behavior is absent and operation ordering is inconsistent: editing says persist then rebuild, importing says rebuild and persist, and no rollback rule defines whether a failed save leaves the active key map changed. The skills flow contains an explicit failure-state rule that shortcuts lack.

Key-event capture and propagation remain consequential implementation choices. All events must pass through the key map, yet capture may be central or per-widget and may occur at window or focused-widget level; consumption, fallback to native text behavior, and precedence are not fixed.
First-wins skill deduplication lacks an exact search order. The listed root precedence is exemplary rather than normative, so duplicate-name winners can differ across conforming implementations.

Skill mutation collision policies remain open for a pre-existing directory without SKILL.md, concurrent disk edits, and frontmatter name changes. These choices determine overwrite, partial-state recovery, prompting, and directory rename behavior.

Ask is an accepted permission value and permission state contributes to pre-launch readiness, but its runtime prompt is deferred to phase 2. The current allow, deny, block-readiness, or prompt behavior for Ask is therefore unspecified.
Validate-all presentation is internally inconsistent: a full table is declared the decision and repeated as acceptance behavior, yet an errors-only modal remains permitted for v1.

Validate-all scope conflicts with first-wins discovery. The feature is titled as validating all SKILL.md files on disk, but its algorithm validates only discover_skills results, while later duplicate names may be skipped; shadowed invalid files may therefore escape validation.

Bulk-permission persistence has two non-equivalent permitted models: store one pattern rule or materialize explicit entries for every current match. Because explicit entries outrank patterns, these models differ for later edits, future skills, and subsequent bulk rules.

Compatible import roots lack an exact source classification for list filtering. Discovery includes PM and compatible roots, but the required source filter exposes only Project and Global, leaving provider/account-local or other compatible roots unmapped.

The post-execution process contract is incomplete: cleanup_after_execution requires a pid and includes process termination, but the mandated execution-engine call passes literal 0 without defining whether 0 is a sentinel or which process is to be terminated.

Cleanup defaults are unspecified. CleanupConfig contains flags capable of removing untracked, ignored, output, or build-artifact data, while the execution engine uses unwrap_or_default without defining the four default booleans.

Cleanup coverage for app.rs execute_ai_turn is explicitly optional even when a project working directory is known, allowing otherwise conforming implementations to apply different pre/post-run hygiene to the same execution path.

Evidence-retention behavior remains unresolved because retain_last_runs is required but the definition of a run is deferred, with an alternative suggestion to prefer retention_days. Implementers cannot produce equivalent pruning decisions.

Per-platform skill delivery is not implementation-exact in this window. The MVP names registry, permission filtering, context bundling, and the skill tool, but platform_specs must still choose paths versus content and transport, and the backend is allowed to remain a stub until that authority exists.
Skill preview representation is not exact: acceptance says the body appears, while the GUI contract permits either markdown body without frontmatter or the full file with collapsed frontmatter.

explicit_non_gaps.summary: Invalid or unparseable shortcut configuration has an explicit non-crashing fallback, warning, and user-facing toast.
Shortcut empty-filter, no-match, and not-yet-loaded presentation states are explicitly distinguished and exclude undefined-looking labels.
Required and optional skill tool-reference failures have distinct readiness and warning semantics, and the GUI must preserve exact failing references.
Workspace-owned projections are kept distinct from provider runtime state, and projection failure does not imply PM-native runtime failure.
Explicit per-skill permission entries unambiguously take precedence over pattern rules.
Validate-all is read-only, reuses load validation, reports per-skill errors, and continues after an unreadable file instead of aborting the batch.
Post-execution cleanup is explicitly forbidden from invoking git clean; git-clean behavior is confined to preparation and the manual cleanup action.
Clearing agent output removes contents only, preserves the directory, and evidence pruning is excluded from cleanup_after_execution.
Cleanup allowlist and git-clean logic are explicitly centralized under src/cleanup.

unknowns.summary: The exact ShortcutAction universe and default rows cannot be established from authoritative core lines; the only pointer in the permitted window is context-before text referring to the §7.7 table.
The canonical compatible skill roots, their exact precedence, and wildcard semantics are defined outside this window and were not inspected.
The exact per-platform skill transport contract remains in platform_specs or an orchestrator plan outside the allowed window.
The full cleanup exclusion list and §4.8 process/build-artifact details are outside the allowed window; this window only requires their reuse and verification.
Whether skill frontmatter actually adopts a version field, and its schema if adopted, is not fixed here.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: Merge defaults with overrides (overrides take precedence).
On app startup, load GuiConfig, build key map, install into the app's key event handler.
All key events (e.g. in composer, prompt fields) go through this map to resolve to `ShortcutAction` then execute the corresponding behavior.
update GuiConfig.shortcuts and persist; then rebuild key map so the new binding is active immediately.
(1) On app startup after loading GuiConfig; (2) After user saves a change on the Shortcuts screen (edit or reset); (3) After successful import (Replace or Merge).
If it fails to parse or is invalid, fall back to empty overrides, log warning, show toast "Shortcuts reset to defaults due to config error" (§7.11).
Use `validate_shortcut_binding` to reject duplicate action binding (same key bound to two actions); optionally warn on system shortcut.
discover skills from PM roots plus compatible import roots defined by the canonical skill system.
`required_tool_refs` problems block runnable `/readiness`, `optional_tool_refs` problems warn, and the Skills `GUI` surfaces the exact failing refs instead of flattening them into one generic error.
compute runtime readiness before launch from validation state, permission state, and tool availability.
bundle PM-selected skill content into the compiled context.
expose the PM `skill` tool for on-demand skill retrieval during the run.

workspace-owned projections are tracked separately from provider-root-owned runtime state; cleanup or repair flows must not confuse workspace-owned projected files with provider-root-owned account/runtime directories.
a projection failure does not mean PM-native skill runtime delivery failed.
This subsection closes open decisions and documents gaps so an **implementation plan** can be derived without ambiguity.
Implementation plan should enumerate and wire key map in one central place (e.g. app-level key subscription) or per-widget; prefer central so behavior is consistent.
Slint: use a `FocusScope` (or window-level `key-pressed` handler) at the appropriate level (window or focused widget).
If supporting macOS, map Ctrl -> Cmd and Alt -> Option when reading/writing config or displaying in GUI; do this in one place (same DRY data or a small platform module).
use a format that is cross-platform and stable (e.g. string `"Ctrl+A"` or structured `{ "modifiers": ["ctrl"], "key": "A" }`).

if the key combo is already bound to a *different* action, either (a) **reject** with tooltip "Already used by <ActionName>" and do not save, or (b) **steal** (assign to new action and remove from old); implementation must decide.

Export JSON must include a `version` field (e.g. `1`). On import, if `version` is missing or greater than the highest supported version, **reject** with message "Unsupported shortcut file version" (or "implementation must decide": skip unknown version and attempt to parse known fields for best-effort import).
Discovery walks paths in a defined order (e.g. project paths first, then global; within each, e.g. `.puppet-master/skills` then `.claude/skills` then `.agents/skills`).
Implementation must decide whether to treat "dir exists but no SKILL.md" as error or as partial state (e.g. offer to create SKILL.md only).

If the user has the skill open in the GUI editor and the file is changed on disk (e.g. by another editor or process), on save: (1) overwrite and warn "File was modified on disk; your version was saved", or (2) detect mtime/content change and prompt "File changed on disk. Reload / Overwrite / Cancel", or (3) lock file for v1 (complex).

**Decision:** Show a **full table** (all discovered skills) with a status column: OK or Error + message. This allows users to see which skills passed and which failed in one view. Summary line: "N OK, M errors." Optional: filter toggle "Show only errors" to collapse to errors-only. Implementation plan may choose errors-only modal for v1 if full table is deferred.
Implementation plan can mark "ask" as phase 2 and leave exact UI location to implementation.
Explicit per-skill entry wins over pattern.

On save, if user changes `name` in frontmatter so it no longer matches the dir name: (1) reject with validation error "Name must match folder name", or (2) offer "Rename folder" to rename dir to match (then save). Prefer (1) for v1 to avoid accidental renames.
MVP runtime delivery uses the canonical registry + permission filter + context bundling + `skill` tool path.
User can export current overrides to a JSON file and import from file with Replace/Merge and validation.
Serialize current overrides only (or full key map) to JSON.
On success, rebuild key map and persist; toast "Imported N shortcuts."
Unknown action id in file → skip or reject entire import; document to skip unknown and import known only, or reject with "Unknown action: X".
if invalid, reject with "Conflict: key already used by <Action>" or apply and steal; implementation must decide (recommend reject).

Empty filter shows all rows. When filter is non-empty and no row matches, show empty list plus a single inline message (e.g. "No shortcuts match '...'") so the user distinguishes "no match" from "no shortcuts loaded."
**When key map not yet loaded** (e.g. config not loaded at init): show action label only (no key suffix) or placeholder "(Loading...)"; never show blank or "(undefined)".

User enters pattern (e.g. `doc-*`) and selects Allow/Deny/Ask; Apply shows confirmation with count; on confirm, config is updated and persisted; list reflects new permissions; explicit per-skill overrides pattern (see precedence below).
add or update pattern entry (e.g. `"doc-*": "allow"`) or set per-skill entries for each match.
**Explicit per-skill wins over pattern** (so "doc-release" with explicit "deny" is still denied when pattern "doc-*" is allow).
If config persist fails after Apply, show error toast; do not update in-memory state as "saved" so user can retry.
filter by text (name/description), source (All / Project / Global), and permission (All / Allow / Deny / Ask)
sort and filter apply in-memory to that list; no re-discovery on sort/filter change.
Selecting a skill in the list shows its body in a read-only pane (Skills tab); content is load-on-demand; user can copy text; "Edit" opens full editor.
Content = markdown body only (no frontmatter), or full file with frontmatter collapsed.
If `load_skill` fails for selected skill (e.g. file deleted on disk), show message in preview pane (e.g. "Could not load skill: ...") and optionally refresh list.
If frontmatter supports an optional `version` field (or under `metadata.version`), parse and show in list or preview.
all discovered skills are validated; results show in a full table (all skills) with status OK or Error + message; summary "N OK, M errors"; errors are copy-pasteable (selectable labels).
Show results in a **full table** (all discovered skills) with status column: OK or Error + message
No write; read-only. Reuse validation logic from load_skill to avoid duplication.
do not abort entire run -- continue and report per-skill.
